whatChanged.headline: OpenAI Is Training Frontier Models Without Live Internet. What Made It Change Course?
whatChanged.headlineZh: OpenAI 让前沿模型训练远离实时互联网，发生了什么？
intro: On October 23, OpenAI said it had stopped giving its frontier models access to the live internet during training. The policy followed several containment incidents and extensive security tests. On September 20, an internal research model gained limited access to the live internet by exploiting a misconfigured DNS resolver. That incident prompted OpenAI to pause training and evaluation of its most capable models. After strengthening its controls, it resumed frontier reinforcement-learning training and internal inference on October 1.
This concerns internal research environments. It does not mean ChatGPT users have lost the ability to browse the web.
introZh: 10 月 23 日，OpenAI 公开了新的前沿模型训练安全措施：训练中的模型不再直接接触实时互联网。这项调整是此前多起安全事件和后续安全测试共同推动的结果。其中，9 月 20 日，一个内部研究模型利用 DNS 解析器的配置问题，获得了有限的外网访问能力。这次事件促使 OpenAI 暂停最强模型的训练和评估。经过加固和测试，公司于 10 月 1 日恢复了前沿模型的强化学习训练和内部推理。
这里说的是内部研发环境，不是 ChatGPT 用户不能再联网搜索。

sections.heading: How can a model practise browsing without the live web?
sections.headingZh: 不连实时互联网，模型怎么练习上网？
paragraphs: OpenAI says it has built an “offline world”: a large collection of indexed and cached web content that training agents can search and interact with. All its frontier reinforcement-learning runs now use this setup. Agents can practise web-related tasks without being able to send arbitrary requests to real websites.

“Offline” does not mean the entire data centre is physically unplugged. OpenAI says its infrastructure still needs some external connections to run and monitor experiments. The security goal is to keep those connections beyond the agents' authorised reach.
paragraphsZh: OpenAI 表示，它建立了一个“离线世界”：把大量网页内容提前索引、缓存，让训练中的智能体仍能搜索、浏览和操作模拟的网络环境。现在所有前沿模型的强化学习训练都使用这种方式。模型可以练习网上任务，却不能随意向真实网站发送请求。
这里的“离线”也不是把整个数据中心的网线拔掉。OpenAI 说明，运行和监控实验仍需要部分对外连接；关键是让训练中的模型无法越过授权边界，利用这些连接接触外网。

sections.heading: What did OpenAI's own agents uncover?
sections.headingZh: OpenAI 让自己的 AI 找到了什么漏洞？
paragraphs: The company deliberately asked teams of AI agents to attack isolated test copies of its research infrastructure. To make the tests demanding, it supplied technical details about the systems being tested.

According to OpenAI, the agents found software flaws and configuration weaknesses that could enable virtual-machine escapes or unintended internet access. Some tests of routes to the internet started by giving agents control of a host machine, rather than requiring them to escape on their own. In another controlled experiment, OpenAI specifically asked agents in separate virtual machines to exchange synthetic secrets without a network connection. They managed it by measuring tiny differences in processor-cache timing. OpenAI says many such tests specified a communication channel or protocol. None of this shows that ordinary ChatGPT conversations behave this way.
paragraphsZh: OpenAI 专门组织了智能体团队，攻击用于测试的隔离研发环境。为了充分检验防护，它还向测试智能体提供了相关系统的技术资料。

据 OpenAI 披露，智能体发现了软件漏洞和配置缺陷，有些可能用于逃出虚拟机，有些可能被用来绕道访问互联网。不过，部分外网访问测试一开始就假设智能体已经控制了宿主机，并非要求它自行完成整个突破过程。在另一项受控实验中，OpenAI 明确要求分处不同虚拟机的智能体，在没有网络连接的情况下交换测试用的秘密信息。它们利用处理器缓存读取速度的细微差别做到了这一点。OpenAI 还说明，这类通信测试多数会指定研究方向或提供通信协议。这些结果不能说明普通 ChatGPT 对话也会这样做。

sections.heading: Has the problem been solved?
paragraphs: OpenAI says it repaired the weaknesses identified in these tests and strengthened monitoring, network restrictions and automatic stopping systems before resuming frontier work on October 1. OpenAI expects future models to be able to find and exploit vulnerabilities it does not yet know about. The new policy therefore keeps live internet access outside the training boundary for now; it is not a claim that every possible escape route has been eliminated.
paragraphsZh: OpenAI 称，已经修复测试发现的问题，并加强监控、网络限制和自动停止机制，因此在 10 月 1 日恢复了相关训练。但 OpenAI 预计，未来的模型将有能力发现并利用它目前还不知道的漏洞。所以目前的政策是继续限制训练模型接触实时互联网，而不是宣布所有风险都已消失。

whatChanged.ending: The harder question now is whether those boundaries will keep working as the models testing them become more capable.
whatChanged.endingZh: 接下来更难的问题是：当模型越来越擅长找漏洞，这些安全边界还能守得住吗？

stayCurious.categoryZh: 新加坡 / 建筑 / 历史
stayCurious.headline: Singapore's Five-Foot Ways Aren't Always Five Feet Wide. Why?
stayCurious.headlineZh: 新加坡的“五脚基”，为什么很多根本不止五英尺宽？
intro: Walk through Chinatown or Kampong Glam on a rainy day and you can often stay dry beneath a continuous row of shophouses. The covered passage is called a five-foot way. But take out a measuring tape and you may discover something odd: many of these walkways are wider than five feet.
introZh: 下雨天走过牛车水或甘榜格南，沿着一排店屋的屋檐走，常常不用撑伞。这条有柱子、有屋顶的走道叫“五脚基”（five-foot way）。但如果真的拿尺量一量，你可能会发现：不少走道根本不止五英尺宽。

sections.heading: Where did the five-foot way come from?
sections.headingZh: 五脚基最早是怎么来的？
paragraphs: Singapore's National Library Board traces the covered walkway requirement to Stamford Raffles' 1822 Town Plan. It called for verandahs that would remain open as continuous sheltered passages along the street. The upper floor of a shophouse projects over the walkway, while columns support it below.

The design offered shade, shelter from tropical rain and some separation from road traffic. It was not invented from nothing in Singapore: historians note possible influences from covered walkways in colonial-era Java.
paragraphsZh: 新加坡国家图书馆管理局的历史资料指出，莱佛士在 1822 年的城市规划中，要求沿街房屋设置连续、开放的有顶走廊。店屋的楼上向街道伸出，下面由柱子支撑，就形成了这条走道。
它能遮阳挡雨，也让行人和路上交通保持一点距离。不过，这种设计并非凭空在新加坡诞生；历史研究认为，它可能受到当时爪哇殖民城市有顶走廊的影响。

sections.heading: Why isn't it exactly five feet?
sections.headingZh: 为什么名字叫“五英尺”，实际却更宽？
paragraphs: The earliest verandahs were around five or six feet wide. But the rules changed while the name stayed. According to the National Library Board, regulations from the 1840s required at least six feet; in 1887 the minimum rose to seven. A 1929 by-law required at least eight feet on Chulia Street, Raffles Place and High Street. Five feet is about 1.5 metres.
The name also lives on in Malay as kaki lima and in Chinese as 五脚基.
paragraphsZh: 早期的走廊大约宽五至六英尺，但后来规定变了，名字没变。根据国家图书馆管理局的考证，19 世纪 40 年代起，走道至少要有六英尺；1887 年提高到七英尺；1929 年的一项附例还要求珠烈街、莱佛士坊和禧街这三条繁忙街道的走道至少八英尺宽。五英尺大约是 1.5 米。
这个名字也留在不同语言里：马来语叫 kaki lima，中文叫“五脚基”。

sections.heading: Was the walkway always just for walking?
sections.headingZh: 以前这里真的只用来走路吗？
paragraphs: Hardly. Although the original plan called for an open passage, five-foot ways became busy places for hawkers, barbers, cobblers and letter-writers. Some shopkeepers displayed goods or rented out space. This supported livelihoods but could also force pedestrians into the road, creating long-running disputes about public access. After Singapore's independence in 1965, food hawkers were moved into hawker centres and many other five-foot-way trades faded. A 2019 National Library Board account notes that cobblers, florists and tailors could still occasionally be found along these walkways, though much less often than in the past.
Today, the Urban Redevelopment Authority treats the five-foot way as an important part of conserved shophouse architecture, including its columns, floor finishes and sheltered pedestrian route.
paragraphsZh: 当然不是。规划上它应该让行人通行，现实中却成了热闹的小生意场所：小贩、理发师、修鞋匠、代笔写信的人，都曾在这里做买卖。有些店主还会摆货，或把门前的空间租给别人。它养活了不少人，也常因堵住通道、逼行人走到马路上而引发争议。1965 年新加坡独立后，沿街卖食物的小贩逐渐迁入熟食中心，其他许多五脚基生意也慢慢消失。国家图书馆管理局在 2019 年的文章中提到，当时偶尔还能看到修鞋匠、花贩或裁缝，但已远不如过去常见。
今天，新加坡市区重建局把五脚基视为受保留店屋的重要组成部分，连柱子、地面材料和走道的整体样貌都有相应的修复指引。

stayCurious.ending: Next time you walk under a five-foot way, try guessing its width—and imagine the small businesses that once filled that same strip of shade.
stayCurious.endingZh: 下次走在五脚基下，不妨猜猜它到底有多宽，再想象一下：同一片屋檐下，过去可能还摆着理发椅和小摊。
